summary: F1: A phishing-suspect payroll IBAN-correction email was delivered to n.guler@aegean.edu from aegean-edu.com.tr; no follow-on signals survived the clean monitoring window.

timeline.event: F1 Phishing-suspect mail delivered from aegean-edu.com.tr (subject=Ekim maaş bordrosu düzeltmesi – IBAN güncelleme)

findings.claim: Phishing-suspect mail delivered from aegean-edu.com.tr (subject=Ekim maaş bordrosu düzeltmesi – IBAN güncelleme)

actions.action: Advise the user not to click links, reply, or enter credentials; delete the message and report via the SOC phishing mailbox.
Block aegean-edu.com.tr and the message subject at the secure email gateway; add sender to blocklist.
Search historical mail logs for the same sender/subject across other @aegean.edu users and quarantine any matches.
Monitor the affected mailbox for 30 days for inbox rules, MFA changes, or impossible travel.

limitations: Confidence relies solely on F1; no additional corroborating telemetry survived the clean window.
not_checked: EDR telemetry and authentication logs beyond the follow-up window were not reviewed.

contrastive.explanation: Rejecting F1 as unsupported would leave zero surviving signals and the policy would call this benign.

risk.rationale: Verified evidence only: F1 confirms delivery of a phishing-suspect email (T1566.002) with a salary/IBAN-update subject. There is no confirmed credential compromise, no account-takeover chain, no rejected claims explaining the signal away, and no data-quality conflicts. Therefore contain is not supported, benign is not supported, and there is no conflict/exposure requiring escalation; treat as an isolated unexplained signal and monitor for follow-on authentication or IBAN change activity.
